Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates bilateral widening of the lower posterior mediastinum with smooth, lateral displacement of both paraspinal lines (indicated by arrowheads) and no evidence of vertebral destruction. This radiographic appearance is characteristic of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (or similar lymphoproliferative disorders) presenting as paravertebral masses, distinguishing it from neurogenic tumors which are typically unilateral and abscesses which often show bone erosion.
